why: The STM32, the IMU and both motor drivers' logic sides run from this rail; below 3.1 V the MCU browns out mid-drive.
Both DRV8833s take motor current straight off this rail; a sagging VBAT is torque the rover does not have.
R1 is the STM32's reset pull-up. If it is tied to the wrong net or missing, NRST floats and the MCU resets at random — the single most common cause of a rover that drives for ten seconds and stops.
R2 limits the power LED. A wrong decade here is either an invisible LED or one drawing 15 mA off the logic rail the MCU is trying to run from.
